title: SF424 Mandatory Form
description: SF424 Mandatory Form (SF424_Mandatory_3_0) is a streamlined variant of the SF-424 used for formula grants, block grants, and other mandatory awards. Unlike the standard SF-424, it includes submission type, frequency, version, and consolidated request fields, but has a reduced estimated funding section (Federal and Match only, versus 7 line items on the standard SF-424).
notes: Separate form definition composed from existing organization/name/address/phone/email/opportunity/person/certification questions. Contact and authorized representative are separate answers; no unrequested contact addresses.
Opportunity-owned agency/listing fields are nested under opportunity, with assistance_listing as a child, as a proposed grouping for review. Exact paths remain a candidate for family review.

Applicant organization and EIN are required by the DAT even though Organization/EIN are optional in the XSD. This candidate follows the DAT for applicant entry while preserving the source XML structure; this is recorded for review.

Other submission type, other frequency, consolidated request, other applicant type, available state review and delinquent debt have six conditionally required dependent fields. Disabled does not imply a global answer-clearing policy.
Received date, signature and signature date are optional in draft answers and supplied on submission. Agency/listing and UEI are read-only pre-populated using existing API providers.

The 250-character project title and 30-character department/division limits differ from the current 200/100-character question-bank contracts. Local primitive constraints are explicit; shared bank questions are not copied, tightened or silently widened.

Supporting documents are an optional ordered list of up to 100 uploaded file UUIDs; additional congressional districts is a separate single UUID. Actual file name/MIME/location/hash and ownership belong to existing upload/API services.
Budget amounts preserve the XSD range 0..999999999999.99 and two-decimal contract. Decimal admission/serialization is verified separately from static facets.

The layout groups applicant type with the applicant organization and groups received dates together. This deliberate display-order difference keeps each semantic object placed once; source XML sequence is unchanged.
risks: US postal validation accepts five digits, but the DAT requires nine. A reviewed ZIP+4 rule belongs in shared Address; this form does not change that rule.

Changing Country can leave both State and Province in an answer. GlobalLibrary permits only one, so that answer fails XSD validation. Shared Address/retention behavior needs a reviewed fix before API submission; this form does not clear answers or change XML handling.
Preview attachment UUID examples are illustrative, not uploaded files. Browser/deployed/Grantor1/training/PDF and final signing gates remain separate from compilation/API fixtures.
Opportunity paths, organization requiredness and all source choices are reviewable candidates, not human policy acceptance.

The maintained API multipleOf validator rejects source-valid numeric amounts 0.29 and 1.15 at multipleOf 0.01 because of floating arithmetic. Preserve the source precision constraint; consumer precision needs resolution before API readiness.

State-review options currently carry source codes StateReviewAvailable/StateReviewNotSelected/StateReviewNotNeeded. Source-readable option labels need rendered qualification and an agreed existing-library route; no private enum/renderer adapter is introduced.
The DAT burden-statement row cites OMB 4040-0002 while Form Info and the PDF header identify 4040-0020. This candidate follows the latter and retains the source conflict for review.

18. By signing this application, I certify (1) to the statements contained in the list of certifications** and (2) that the statements herein are true, complete and accurate to the best of my knowledge. I also provide the required assurances** and agree to comply with any resulting terms if I accept an award. I am aware that any false, fictitious, or fraudulent statements or claims may subject me to criminal, civil, or administrative penalties. (U.S. Code, Title 18, Section 1001)

** This list of certifications and assurances, or an internet site where you may obtain this list, is contained in the announcement or agency specific instructions.
